item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"Candidate A follows the frozen contract directly and with minimal scope, while Candidate B explicitly violates key requirements by duplicating Files.Add and changing global request-body/retry behavior.","reasons":["A reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\" and delegates to s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), preserving centralized option handling, request construction, decoding, and errors.","A preserves FilesService.Add unchanged and confines the production change to the requested Upload convenience API.","B reimplements Files.Add logic inside Upload instead of routing through Add, creating duplicate machinery and violating an explicit contract requirement.","B modifies RawClient.Do to buffer broadly scoped io.Reader bodies, changing Add, Update, and unrelated requests despite the contract forbidding unrelated retry refactoring and requiring Add behavior to remain unchanged. This can also unexpectedly buffer very large bodies whenever WithNoRetry is absent, even if a request will not actually be retried."],"risks_a":["Tests do not cover empty-filename/nil-content validation or source-reader failures, both explicitly requested.","The retry test does not set RetryAllMethods: true or verify that multipart content is intact on every attempt, so its verification of the reported scenario is weaker than B's.","Validation combines two distinct invalid inputs into one generic error, though both are still rejected before request creation."],"risks_b":["Upload duplicates Files.Add internals and can drift from its API and error semantics.","Global reader buffering is an unauthorized behavioral and memory-use change affecting the entire SDK.","The added documentation advertises broader Add/Update retry behavior that the frozen contract specifically excludes from this change."]}
